A unit positive test charge placed at that point

At an angle of 30° to the field
Perpendicular to the magnetic field lines

questions.text: The device used to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy is an

The physical dimensions of the cathode
The excess frequency above the threshold
questions.explanation: Maximum kinetic energy equals h(f - f_0), scaling directly with frequency beyond threshold.

questions.text: X-rays differ from ultraviolet rays primarily because X-rays have
questions.explanation: X-rays sit higher on the electromagnetic spectrum with greater photon energy, higher frequency, and shorter wavelength.

questions.text: The energy equivalent of a mass defect of 0.005 amu is approximately

questions.text: Doping an intrinsic semiconductor with a trivalent impurity creates an
questions.explanation: Trivalent dopants (like boron or indium) accept electrons, generating mobile holes characteristic of p-type materials.

questions.text: Which logic gate yields a high output (1) only when all its inputs are high (1)?
questions.explanation: An AND gate requires every input to be 1 to produce a high output.

questions.text: Newton's second law of motion establishes a quantitative relation between force and
questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that applied force equals the time rate of change of linear momentum.

Friction is completely absent from air
No external net force acts on the system

questions.text: The center of gravity of a uniform triangular lamina is located at its

questions.text: The hydraulic press operates on the principle formulated by

questions.text: The SI unit of dynamic viscosity can be expressed in terms of fundamental units as

questions.text: Absolute zero temperature on the Kelvin scale is defined as

questions.text: The dimensions of gravitational potential energy are

questions.text: A stone is thrown horizontally from the top of a tower with a speed of 15 m/s. If it hits the ground after 4 s, the height of the tower is (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Vertical height h = ½gt² = 0.5 × 10 × (4)² = 5 × 16 = 80 m.

questions.text: Which of the following physical quantities is a scalar?
questions.explanation: Electric flux is a scalar product of electric field and area vector, yielding a scalar quantity.

The S.I. unit of specific heat capacity is

questions.text: During a phase change from liquid to gas at boiling point, the added thermal energy is used exclusively to
questions.explanation: Latent heat of vaporization goes into breaking intermolecular bonds rather than increasing kinetic temperature.

questions.text: The quantity of heat given out when 50 g of water cools from 80 °C to 30 °C (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J/g°C) is
Conduction is the primary mode of heat transfer in
questions.explanation: Solids transfer thermal energy predominantly via conduction through lattice vibrations and free electrons.

questions.text: According to Charles's law, the volume of a given mass of gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to its
questions.explanation: Charles's law states that V ∝ T when pressure remains constant, provided temperature is measured in Kelvin.

questions.text: An organ pipe closed at one end has a length of 0.85 m. Taking the speed of sound in air as 340 m/s, its fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency for a closed pipe f = v / (4L) = 340 / (4 × 0.85) = 340 / 3.4 = 100 Hz.

questions.text: The phenomenon of bending of light waves around the edges of an obstacle is known as
questions.explanation: Diffraction describes wave spreading when encountering obstacles or apertures comparable to their wavelength.

questions.text: The loudness of a musical sound depends directly on the
questions.explanation: Wave amplitude governs sound intensity and the subjective perception of loudness.

questions.text: An object is placed 12 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 8 cm. The image distance is
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/8 − 1/12 = (3 − 2)/24 = 1/24, so v = 24 cm. The image is real and in front of the mirror.

questions.text: The absolute refractive index of a transparent medium is 4/3. The speed of light in this medium is
Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from
options: Glass into air at an angle greater than critical angle
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection requires incidence from a denser medium to a rarer medium beyond the critical angle threshold.

questions.text: A person with hypermetropia (long-sightedness) focuses near objects
questions.explanation: Hypermetropia causes weak eye refraction, forming images behind the retina for close objects.

questions.text: The SI unit of capacitance is the
questions.explanation: Electrical capacitance is measured in Farads (F).

questions.text: The electric field intensity at a distance r from a point charge Q is expressed as
questions.explanation: Coulomb's electric field follows an inverse-square law: E = kQ / r².

questions.text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 5 Ω are connected in series across a 20 V battery. The total current in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Total resistance R = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω. Current I = V / R = 20 / 10 = 2 A.

questions.text: In a meter bridge experiment, the null point is obtained at 60 cm from the left end. The ratio of the left resistance to the right resistance is
questions.explanation: Bridge resistance ratio equals length ratio: R_l / R_r = l_l / l_r = 60 / 40 = 3 / 2.

questions.text: The magnetic force acting on a moving charge q with velocity v parallel to a magnetic field B is
questions.explanation: Since F = qvB sin(θ) and sin(0°) = 0 for parallel motion, the magnetic force is zero.

questions.text: The conversion of electrical energy into mechanical energy is achieved using an
questions.explanation: Electric motors utilize current-carrying conductors in magnetic fields to generate rotational mechanical motion.

In an alternating current circuit containing a pure inductor, the current
options: Is completely in phase with voltage

questions.explanation: Einstein's relation: KE_max = E - W = 3.5 eV - 2.0 eV = 1.5 eV.

questions.text: X-rays are high-frequency electromagnetic waves characterized by being
options: Uncharged and unaffected by electric or magnetic fields
questions.explanation: X-rays are uncharged electromagnetic photons, meaning external electric and magnetic fields leave them undeflected.

questions.text: The mass defect in a nuclear reaction is 0.01 amu. The energy released is approximately
questions.explanation: Energy released = 0.01 amu × 931.5 MeV/amu ≈ 9.32 MeV (approx 9.31 MeV).

questions.text: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is 5 days. What fraction of the original sample disintegrates after 15 days?
questions.explanation: After 3 half-lives (15 days), the remaining fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8. Therefore, the fraction disintegrated is 1 - (1/8) = 7/8.

questions.text: Doping pure germanium with a trivalent impurity such as indium creates
questions.explanation: Trivalent dopants introduce electron holes, producing p-type semiconductor characteristics.

questions.text: Which logic gate produces a low (0) output only when all its inputs are high (1)?
questions.explanation: A NAND gate outputs 0 exclusively when every input is 1.

questions.text: Newton's first law of motion provides a quantitative definition for
questions.explanation: Newton's first law establishes the principle of inertia, describing how objects maintain their motion state.

The conservation of linear momentum during an explosion or collision is a direct result of
questions.explanation: Equal and opposite action-reaction forces (Newton's third law) ensure internal impulses cancel out, conserving total momentum.

questions.text: The center of gravity of a uniform solid sphere is located at its

questions.text: The relationship between volume expansivity γ and linear expansivity α for a solid is
questions.explanation: Cubic volume thermal expansion coefficient γ is approximately three times the linear expansivity α.

questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 K) is equal to -273.15 °C.

questions.explanation: The spatial separation between adjacent nodes or antinodes in standing waves is half a wavelength (λ/2).

questions.explanation: Fringe width w = λD / d shows direct proportionality to screen distance D, so increasing D increases fringe separation.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following reduces parallax error when reading a measuring instrument?

Placing the eye directly above the reading

topic_questions.explanation: Least count = pitch ÷ number of divisions = 0.5 mm ÷ 50 = 0.01 mm.

topic_questions.explanation: Measurements that are close to one another demonstrate precision.

topic_questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder is commonly used to measure the volume of a liquid.

topic_questions.text: A car travels 120 m in 10 s. What is its average speed?
topic_questions.explanation: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 120 m ÷ 10 s = 12 m/s.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
topic_questions.explanation: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector quantity.

topic_questions.text: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² for 5 s. What is its final velocity?
topic_questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, v = 0 + (4 × 5) = 20 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A body moving with uniform velocity has
topic_questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means both speed and direction remain constant, so acceleration is zero.

topic_questions.text: A car moving at 20 m/s comes to rest in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
topic_questions.explanation: Acceleration = (v - u) ÷ t = (0 - 20) ÷ 5 = -4 m/s².

topic_questions.text: The slope of a distance-time graph represents
topic_questions.explanation: The slope of a distance-time graph gives speed.

topic_questions.text: A body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. Its motion is described as
topic_questions.explanation: Uniform motion occurs when equal distances are covered in equal time intervals.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following equations is correct for uniformly accelerated motion?
topic_questions.explanation: The correct equation for uniformly accelerated motion is v² = u² + 2as.

topic_questions.text: A runner completes one full lap of a circular track and returns to the starting point. What is the displacement?
topic_questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line distance from the initial to final position. Since both positions are the same, displacement is zero.

topic_questions.text: A body travels 30 m east and then 40 m north. What is the magnitude of its displacement?
topic_questions.explanation: The displacement is the hypotenuse of a right triangle: √(30² + 40²) = 50 m.

topic_questions.text: The area under a velocity-time graph represents
topic_questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement; for motion in one direction, it also gives distance.

topic_questions.text: A vehicle increases its velocity from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 s. Its acceleration is
topic_questions.explanation: Acceleration = (30 - 10) ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

topic_questions.text: A body is said to be at rest when its position
options: does not change with respect to a reference point
topic_questions.explanation: An object is at rest when its position remains unchanged relative to a chosen reference point.

topic_questions.text: A cyclist travels at a constant speed of 8 m/s for 25 s. What distance does the cyclist cover?
topic_questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 8 × 25 = 200 m.

topic_questions.text: A stone is dropped from rest. Ignoring air resistance, its velocity after 3 s is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: Using v = gt, v = 9.8 × 3 = 29.4 m/s.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following quantities can be negative?
topic_questions.explanation: Displacement can be positive or negative depending on the chosen direction.

topic_questions.text: A car travels 60 km in 1.5 hours. Its average speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Average speed = 60 km ÷ 1.5 h = 40 km/h.

topic_questions.text: The acceleration of a body moving with constant velocity is
topic_questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If velocity is constant, acceleration is zero.

topic_questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, 0 = 25 - 5t, so t = 5 s.

topic_questions.text: The velocity of a body changes from 12 m/s east to 12 m/s west in 4 s. Taking east as positive, its acceleration is
topic_questions.explanation: Acceleration = (-12 - 12) ÷ 4 = -6 m/s².

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is the correct SI unit of acceleration?
topic_questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time, so its SI unit is m/s².

topic_questions.text: A body moving at 15 m/s covers a distance of 90 m. How long does it take?
topic_questions.explanation: Time = distance ÷ speed = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 s.

topic_questions.text: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents
topic_questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph is change in velocity divided by time, which is acceleration.

topic_questions.text: A body is projected vertically upward with a velocity of 19.6 m/s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², the maximum height reached is
topic_questions.explanation: At maximum height, v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gh, h = 19.6² ÷ (2 × 9.8) = 19.6 m. Therefore, the correct answer is 19.6 m.

topic_questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes speed from velocity?
options: Speed has direction but velocity does not
Speed is scalar while velocity is vector
topic_questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar quantity, while velocity is a vector quantity.

topic_questions.text: A body travels 20 m in the first 2 s and 30 m in the next 3 s. Its average speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Total distance = 50 m and total time = 5 s. Average speed = 50 ÷ 5 = 10 m/s.

topic_questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, v = 10 + (3 × 4) = 22 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A body moving in a straight line has a velocity of 20 m/s for 5 s. Its displacement is
topic_questions.explanation: Displacement = velocity × time = 20 × 5 = 100 m.

topic_questions.explanation: For uniform acceleration, average velocity = (u + v) ÷ 2 = (4 + 16) ÷ 2 = 10 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A displacement-time graph with a constant positive slope represents
topic_questions.explanation: The slope of a displacement-time graph represents velocity. A constant positive slope therefore indicates constant positive velocity.

topic_questions.explanation: Using v² = u² + 2as, 625 = 225 + 200a, so a = 2 m/s². Therefore, the correct answer is 2 m/s².

topic_questions.text: If a body has zero displacement after a certain time interval, which statement must be true?
options: The body moved and returned to its initial position
The body had zero speed throughout
The body moved only in one direction
topic_questions.explanation: Zero displacement means the final position is the same as the initial position. The body may have moved before returning.

topic_questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward. At its highest point, its
options: velocity and acceleration are both zero
velocity is zero but acceleration is downward
velocity is upward and acceleration is zero
velocity is downward and acceleration is upward
topic_questions.explanation: At the highest point, instantaneous velocity is zero, but gravitational acceleration remains downward.

topic_questions.text: A cyclist travels 3 km east and then 4 km west. What is the magnitude of the displacement?
topic_questions.explanation: Taking east as positive, displacement = 3 - 4 = -1 km. Its magnitude is 1 km.

topic_questions.text: A body has an initial velocity of 10 m/s and acceleration of 2 m/s². What is its velocity after travelling 24 m?
topic_questions.explanation: Using v² = u² + 2as, v² = 10² + 2 × 2 × 24 = 196, so v = 14 m/s. Therefore, the correct answer is 14 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A body moving at 30 m/s is brought to rest with a uniform deceleration of 6 m/s². The distance travelled before stopping is
topic_questions.explanation: Using v² = u² + 2as, 0 = 30² + 2(-6)s. Thus s = 900 ÷ 12 = 75 m.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following best describes instantaneous velocity?
options: Total distance divided by total time
Velocity measured over a very long interval
topic_questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the velocity of a body at a particular instant.

topic_questions.explanation: Total distance = 200 m and total time = 30 s. Average speed = 200 ÷ 30 = 6.67 m/s. Therefore, the correct answer is 6.67 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A particle moves with an acceleration of 5 m/s² from an initial velocity of 3 m/s for 2 s. Its displacement is

topic_questions.text: If the velocity of a body changes uniformly with time, the body has

topic_questions.text: A car moves at 72 km/h. What is its speed in m/s?
Two cars travel in opposite directions at 20 m/s and 15 m/s respectively. Their relative speed is
topic_questions.explanation: For motion in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum: 20 + 15 = 35 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A body moves around a circular track at constant speed. Which quantity changes continuously?
topic_questions.explanation: Although speed remains constant, the direction of motion changes continuously, so velocity changes.

topic_questions.text: A body starts from rest and covers 50 m in 5 s with uniform acceleration. What is its acceleration?
topic_questions.explanation: Using s = 1/2at², 50 = 1/2 × a × 25, so a = 4 m/s².

topic_questions.text: A particle has an initial velocity of 8 m/s and accelerates at 3 m/s² for 4 s. Its final velocity is
topic_questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, v = 8 + (3 × 4) = 20 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A velocity-time graph is a straight line sloping upward from zero. This indicates
topic_questions.explanation: A straight line with a constant positive slope on a velocity-time graph represents uniform positive acceleration.

topic_questions.text: A wave is best described as a
options: disturbance that transfers energy from one point to another
force acting only on stationary objects
form of matter with a fixed mass
topic_questions.explanation: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy from one location to another without a net transfer of matter.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a mechanical wave?
topic_questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave because it requires a material medium for propagation.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following waves can travel through a vacuum?
topic_questions.explanation: Light is an electromagnetic wave and does not require a material medium.

topic_questions.text: The distance between two successive points in phase on a wave is called
topic_questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance between successive points in phase, such as two adjacent crests.

topic_questions.text: The number of complete oscillations made by a wave in one second is called its
topic_questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of complete oscillations per second.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of frequency is
topic_questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz).

topic_questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz. Its period is
topic_questions.explanation: Period T = 1 ÷ f = 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 s.

topic_questions.text: A wave has a period of 0.25 s. Its frequency is
topic_questions.explanation: Frequency f = 1 ÷ T = 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 Hz.

topic_questions.text: The maximum displacement of a particle from its equilibrium position is called
topic_questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the equilibrium position.

topic_questions.text: A wave has a wavelength of 2 m and a frequency of 10 Hz. Its speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 10 × 2 = 20 m/s.

topic_questions.text: A wave travels at 300 m/s and has a frequency of 150 Hz. Its wavelength is
topic_questions.explanation: Wavelength λ = v ÷ f = 300 ÷ 150 = 2 m.

topic_questions.text: Which type of wave has particles vibrating perpendicular to the direction of propagation?
topic_questions.explanation: In a transverse wave, particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction in which the wave travels.

topic_questions.text: In a longitudinal wave, particles vibrate
options: perpendicular to the direction of travel
parallel to the direction of travel
topic_questions.explanation: Particles in a longitudinal wave vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

topic_questions.text: The regions of high pressure in a longitudinal wave are called
topic_questions.explanation: Compressions are regions where particles are closer together and pressure is relatively high.

topic_questions.text: The regions of low pressure in a longitudinal wave are called
topic_questions.explanation: Rarefactions are regions where particles are farther apart and pressure is relatively low.

topic_questions.text: Sound is produced when an object
topic_questions.explanation: Sound is produced by vibrating objects that cause disturbances in the surrounding medium.

topic_questions.text: Sound cannot travel through
topic_questions.explanation: Sound requires a material medium and therefore cannot travel through a vacuum.

topic_questions.text: The speed of sound is generally greatest in
topic_questions.explanation: Sound generally travels fastest through solids because their particles are closely packed.

topic_questions.text: The pitch of a sound depends mainly on its
topic_questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by the frequency of vibration; higher frequency gives higher pitch.

topic_questions.text: The loudness of a sound is related mainly to its
topic_questions.explanation: Greater amplitude generally corresponds to a louder sound.

topic_questions.text: Which characteristic distinguishes a high-pitched sound from a low-pitched sound?
topic_questions.explanation: A high-pitched sound has a higher frequency than a low-pitched sound.

topic_questions.text: An echo is produced mainly by the
topic_questions.explanation: An echo occurs when reflected sound reaches the listener after the original sound.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following surfaces is most suitable for reflecting sound?
topic_questions.explanation: Hard, smooth surfaces reflect sound effectively.

topic_questions.text: A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. How many complete vibrations occur in 4 seconds?
topic_questions.explanation: Number of vibrations = frequency × time = 250 × 4 = 1,000.

topic_questions.text: A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz. Its period is
If the frequency of a wave is doubled while its speed remains constant, its wavelength will
topic_questions.explanation: Since v = fλ and speed is constant, doubling frequency makes wavelength half as large.

topic_questions.text: If the amplitude of a sound wave is increased while its frequency remains constant, the sound becomes
topic_questions.explanation: Increasing amplitude increases the loudness of a sound without changing its pitch.

topic_questions.text: When a wave passes from one medium into another, its frequency generally
topic_questions.explanation: The frequency is determined by the source and normally remains unchanged when a wave enters another medium.

topic_questions.text: Refraction of waves occurs mainly because of a change in their
topic_questions.explanation: Refraction occurs when a wave changes direction because its speed changes as it enters a different medium or region.

topic_questions.text: Diffraction is the
options: bending or spreading of waves around obstacles or through openings
reflection of waves from a surface
production of waves by a source
topic_questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading or bending of waves around obstacles and through openings.

topic_questions.text: Interference occurs when
topic_questions.explanation: Interference occurs when waves overlap and combine to produce a resultant wave.

topic_questions.text: Constructive interference occurs when two waves meet
topic_questions.explanation: Waves meeting in phase reinforce each other, producing constructive interference.

topic_questions.text: Destructive interference occurs when two waves meet
topic_questions.explanation: Waves that meet out of phase can partially or completely cancel each other.

topic_questions.text: A sound wave travels at 340 m/s and has a frequency of 170 Hz. Its wavelength is
A wave has a wavelength of 0.4 m and travels at 200 m/s. Its frequency is
Which of the following is an electromagnetic wave?
topic_questions.explanation: Radio waves are electromagnetic waves and can travel through a vacuum.

topic_questions.text: The human ear normally detects sound frequencies approximately between
topic_questions.explanation: The commonly accepted approximate audible range for humans is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

topic_questions.text: Sound with a frequency above the normal human audible range is called
topic_questions.explanation: Ultrasonic sound has frequencies above approximately 20,000 Hz.

topic_questions.text: Sound with a frequency below the normal human audible range is called
topic_questions.explanation: Infrasonic sound has frequencies below approximately 20 Hz.

topic_questions.text: The phenomenon in which a vibrating body causes another body with the same natural frequency to vibrate strongly is called
topic_questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when a system is driven at or near its natural frequency, producing large amplitude vibrations.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is used to reduce unwanted sound in buildings?
topic_questions.explanation: Soundproofing materials such as thick curtains and acoustic panels help absorb or reduce unwanted sound.

topic_questions.text: The natural frequency of an object is the frequency at which it
topic_questions.explanation: Natural frequency is the frequency at which a system tends to oscillate freely after being disturbed.

topic_questions.text: A sonar system sends a sound pulse toward the seabed and receives the echo after 2 s. If the speed of sound in seawater is 1,500 m/s, the depth of the seabed is
topic_questions.explanation: Total distance travelled = 1,500 × 2 = 3,000 m. The pulse travels down and back, so depth = 3,000 ÷ 2 = 1,500 m.

topic_questions.text: A wave completes 600 oscillations in 3 seconds. Its frequency is
topic_questions.explanation: Frequency = number of oscillations ÷ time = 600 ÷ 3 = 200 Hz.

topic_questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 20 Hz and a wavelength of 3 m. Its speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 20 × 3 = 60 m/s.

topic_questions.text: Which property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
topic_questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by frequency.

topic_questions.text: Which property of a sound wave is most directly associated with its loudness?
topic_questions.explanation: The amplitude of a sound wave is associated with its loudness.

topic_questions.text: A wave travels 120 m in 6 s. Its speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 ÷ 6 = 20 m/s.

topic_questions.text: Which phenomenon explains the spreading of sound around the corner of a building?
topic_questions.explanation: Sound can spread around obstacles because of diffraction.

topic_questions.text: When the frequency of a sound increases, its pitch
topic_questions.explanation: Pitch increases as the frequency of the sound increases.

topic_questions.text: Light is a form of energy that enables the human eye to
topic_questions.explanation: Light enables the eye to see and detect objects.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a natural source of light?
topic_questions.explanation: The Sun is a natural source of visible light.

topic_questions.text: Light travels in a straight line in a
topic_questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines through a uniform transparent medium.

topic_questions.text: The bouncing back of light from a surface is called
topic_questions.explanation: Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface.

topic_questions.text: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of
topic_questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

topic_questions.text: The line drawn perpendicular to a reflecting surface at the point of incidence is called the
topic_questions.explanation: The normal is the line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence.

topic_questions.text: If a ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 30°, the angle of reflection is
topic_questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence, so it is 30°.

topic_questions.text: An object placed 2 m in front of a plane mirror forms an image
options: 2 m in front of the mirror
topic_questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms an image at the same perpendicular distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.

topic_questions.text: The image formed by a plane mirror is
topic_questions.explanation: A plane mirror produces a virtual, upright image of the same size as the object.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the image formed by a plane mirror?
options: It is smaller than the object
topic_questions.explanation: A plane mirror produces lateral inversion, meaning left and right appear reversed.

topic_questions.text: The bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another is called
topic_questions.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of light when it passes between media of different optical densities.

topic_questions.text: When light passes from air into glass, its speed generally
topic_questions.explanation: Light travels more slowly in glass than in air.

topic_questions.text: The refractive index of a medium is related to the
options: speed of light in vacuum and speed of light in the medium
mass and volume of the medium only
topic_questions.explanation: Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed of light in the medium.

topic_questions.text: If the speed of light in a medium is 2 × 10⁸ m/s and its speed in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, the refractive index of the medium is
When light travels from glass into air, it generally bends
options: along the normal in every case
topic_questions.explanation: Light bends away from the normal when it passes from a denser medium such as glass into a less dense medium such as air.

topic_questions.text: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called
topic_questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs when white light separates into its component colours.

topic_questions.text: Which colour of visible light has the longest wavelength?
topic_questions.explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

topic_questions.text: Which colour of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
topic_questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

topic_questions.text: A convex lens is also known as a
topic_questions.explanation: A convex lens converges parallel rays of light and is therefore called a converging lens.

topic_questions.text: A concave lens is also known as a
topic_questions.explanation: A concave lens causes parallel rays to diverge and is therefore called a diverging lens.

topic_questions.text: The point at which parallel rays converge after passing through a convex lens is called the
topic_questions.explanation: The principal focus is the point where rays parallel to the principal axis converge after passing through a convex lens.

topic_questions.text: The distance between the optical centre of a lens and its principal focus is called
topic_questions.explanation: Focal length is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus.

topic_questions.text: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Its power is
topic_questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f in metres = 1/0.20 = 5 D.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of lens power is
topic_questions.explanation: Lens power is measured in dioptres (D).

topic_questions.text: The power of a concave lens is normally
topic_questions.explanation: A concave lens has a negative focal length and therefore negative power.

topic_questions.text: A convex lens can form a real image when the object is placed
options: exactly at its optical centre only
between the lens and its focus only
topic_questions.explanation: A convex lens forms a real image when the object is placed beyond its focal point.

topic_questions.text: When an object is placed between a convex lens and its focal point, the image formed is
topic_questions.explanation: An object within the focal length of a convex lens produces a virtual, upright and magnified image.

topic_questions.text: A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface curves inward is called a
topic_questions.explanation: A concave mirror has a reflecting surface that curves inward.

topic_questions.text: A concave lens generally forms an image that is
topic_questions.explanation: A concave lens normally forms a virtual, upright and diminished image.

topic_questions.text: A convex mirror is commonly used as a vehicle side mirror because it
options: provides a wider field of view
topic_questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives a wider field of view, allowing the driver to see more of the surroundings.

topic_questions.text: The point where the principal axis meets the surface of a spherical mirror is called the
topic_questions.explanation: The pole is the point where the principal axis intersects the mirror surface.

topic_questions.text: The centre of the sphere of which a spherical mirror forms a part is called the
topic_questions.explanation: The centre of curvature is the centre of the sphere from which the spherical mirror is formed.

topic_questions.text: For a spherical mirror, the focal length is
options: equal to the radius of curvature
four times the radius of curvature
topic_questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror, focal length f = R/2.

topic_questions.text: A ray of light passing through the centre of curvature of a concave mirror is reflected
topic_questions.explanation: A ray passing through the centre of curvature strikes the mirror normally and is reflected back along its original path.

topic_questions.text: A ray parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror is reflected through the
topic_questions.explanation: A ray parallel to the principal axis is reflected through the principal focus of a concave mirror.

topic_questions.text: A real image is one that can be
options: formed only by a plane mirror
topic_questions.explanation: A real image is formed by actual convergence of light rays and can be projected onto a screen.

topic_questions.text: A virtual image is formed when light rays
options: actually meet at the image position
appear to come from the image position
topic_questions.explanation: A virtual image is produced when rays do not actually meet but appear to originate from a point.

topic_questions.text: The magnification of an optical system is defined as the ratio of
options: object distance to image distance only
topic_questions.explanation: Magnification is the ratio of image height to object height.

topic_questions.text: If an object is 2 cm high and its image is 6 cm high, the magnification is
topic_questions.explanation: Magnification = image height ÷ object height = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

topic_questions.text: The phenomenon responsible for the formation of a rainbow is mainly
topic_questions.explanation: Rainbows result from refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.

topic_questions.text: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels
options: from a less dense medium to a denser medium at any angle
from a denser medium to a less dense medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
from air to glass at normal incidence
topic_questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser to a less dense medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.

topic_questions.text: Optical fibres transmit light mainly by
topic_questions.explanation: Light signals travel through optical fibres by repeated total internal reflection.

topic_questions.text: The apparent bending of a pencil partly immersed in water is due to
topic_questions.explanation: The pencil appears bent because light from the submerged part is refracted at the water-air boundary.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
topic_questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
topic_questions.explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum.

topic_questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: Light travels in vacuum at approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

topic_questions.text: Which optical device is commonly used to correct short-sightedness?
topic_questions.explanation: Short-sightedness, or myopia, is commonly corrected using a concave lens.

topic_questions.text: Which optical device is commonly used to correct long-sightedness?
topic_questions.explanation: Long-sightedness, or hyperopia, is commonly corrected using a convex lens.

topic_questions.text: When white light passes through a prism, the colour deviated most is
topic_questions.explanation: Violet light is deviated most by a glass prism because it has the shortest wavelength among the visible colours.

topic_questions.text: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a plane mirror. The distance between the object and its image is
topic_questions.explanation: The image is 30 cm behind the mirror, so the object-image distance is 30 + 30 = 60 cm.

topic_questions.text: The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor is called
topic_questions.explanation: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of electric current is
topic_questions.explanation: The ampere (A) is the SI unit of electric current.

topic_questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure electric current in a circuit?
topic_questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in a circuit to measure electric current.

topic_questions.text: A voltmeter is used to measure
topic_questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures the potential difference between two points.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of potential difference is
topic_questions.explanation: Potential difference is measured in volts (V).

topic_questions.text: Ohm's law states that, at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is
options: inversely proportional to the potential difference
directly proportional to the potential difference
topic_questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that current is directly proportional to potential difference when temperature and other physical conditions remain constant.

topic_questions.text: A resistor has a resistance of 4 Ω and carries a current of 3 A. What is the potential difference across it?
topic_questions.explanation: Using V = IR, V = 3 × 4 = 12 V.

topic_questions.text: A 12 V battery is connected to a resistor of 6 Ω. The current in the circuit is
topic_questions.explanation: Using I = V ÷ R, I = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 A.

topic_questions.text: A current of 5 A flows through a 10 Ω resistor. The potential difference across the resistor is
topic_questions.explanation: Using V = IR, V = 5 × 10 = 50 V.

topic_questions.text: The resistance of a conductor depends on its length, cross-sectional area and
topic_questions.explanation: Resistance depends on the material's resistivity as well as the conductor's length and cross-sectional area.

topic_questions.text: For a uniform wire, increasing its length while keeping its cross-sectional area constant will
topic_questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to the length of a uniform conductor.

topic_questions.text: For a uniform wire, increasing its cross-sectional area while keeping its length constant will
topic_questions.explanation: Resistance is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of a uniform wire.

topic_questions.text: The opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of electric current is called
topic_questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is the opposition a conductor offers to current flow.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of electrical resistance is
topic_questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

topic_questions.text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series. Their combined resistance is
topic_questions.explanation: For series resistors, total resistance = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.

topic_questions.text: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. Their effective resistance is
topic_questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω.

topic_questions.text: In a series circuit, the current through each resistor is
topic_questions.explanation: The same current flows through every component in a series circuit.

topic_questions.text: In a parallel circuit, the potential difference across each branch is
topic_questions.explanation: All branches connected in parallel have the same potential difference across them.

topic_questions.text: The electrical power of a device operating at 20 V and carrying 3 A is
topic_questions.explanation: Power P = VI = 20 × 3 = 60 W.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of electrical power is
topic_questions.explanation: Electrical power is measured in watts (W).

topic_questions.text: An electrical appliance rated at 100 W operates for 10 s. The electrical energy consumed is
topic_questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 100 × 10 = 1,000 J.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is the commercial unit of electrical energy?
topic_questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied to consumers is commonly measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh).

topic_questions.text: One kilowatt-hour is equal to
A fuse is connected in a household circuit mainly to
options: protect the circuit from excessive current
topic_questions.explanation: A fuse melts when excessive current flows, breaking the circuit and providing protection.

topic_questions.text: A fuse wire should have a
topic_questions.explanation: A fuse wire is designed to melt quickly when excessive current flows, so it has a relatively low melting point.

topic_questions.text: Which material is commonly used as an electrical conductor?
topic_questions.explanation: Copper is a good electrical conductor and is widely used for electrical wiring.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a good electrical insulator?
topic_questions.explanation: Rubber has very high resistance and is therefore a good electrical insulator.

topic_questions.text: The flow of electrons in a metallic conductor is generally from
options: the centre of the battery outward
the switch to the battery only
topic_questions.explanation: Electrons carry negative charge and move through the external circuit from the negative terminal toward the positive terminal.

topic_questions.text: Conventional current in an external circuit is taken to flow from
options: earth to the positive terminal only
topic_questions.explanation: By convention, current flows from the positive terminal toward the negative terminal through the external circuit.

topic_questions.text: The chemical effect of electric current is used in
topic_questions.explanation: Electroplating uses the chemical effect of electric current to deposit a metal coating.

topic_questions.text: The magnetic effect of electric current is used in an
topic_questions.explanation: An electric motor operates using the force produced on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

topic_questions.text: The heating effect of electric current is used in
topic_questions.explanation: An electric iron converts electrical energy mainly into heat energy.

topic_questions.text: The resistance of an ideal ammeter is
topic_questions.explanation: An ideal ammeter has zero resistance so that it does not significantly alter the current.

topic_questions.text: An ideal voltmeter should have
topic_questions.explanation: A voltmeter should have very high resistance so that it draws negligible current from the circuit.

topic_questions.text: If two identical resistors are connected in series, the effective resistance is
options: half the resistance of one resistor
twice the resistance of one resistor
topic_questions.explanation: Resistances add in series, so two identical resistors give twice the resistance of one.

topic_questions.text: If two identical resistors are connected in parallel, the effective resistance is
options: twice the resistance of one resistor
half the resistance of one resistor
equal to the sum of the resistances
topic_questions.explanation: Two identical resistors connected in parallel have an effective resistance equal to half the resistance of one resistor.

topic_questions.text: A current of 2 A flows through a conductor for 5 s. The charge transferred is
topic_questions.explanation: Charge Q = It = 2 × 5 = 10 C.

topic_questions.text: A charge of 24 C passes through a conductor in 6 s. The current is
topic_questions.explanation: Current I = Q ÷ t = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 A.

topic_questions.text: A 40 W bulb operates at 200 V. The current drawn by the bulb is
topic_questions.explanation: Using P = VI, I = P ÷ V = 40 ÷ 200 = 0.2 A.

topic_questions.text: A resistor connected to a 10 V supply carries a current of 0.5 A. Its resistance is
topic_questions.explanation: Using R = V ÷ I, R = 10 ÷ 0.5 = 20 Ω.

topic_questions.text: When a switch in a simple circuit is open, the circuit is
options: broken and current does not flow
topic_questions.explanation: An open switch breaks the circuit, preventing current from flowing.

topic_questions.text: A short circuit occurs when
options: a very low-resistance path allows excessive current to flow
the circuit contains a large resistor
topic_questions.explanation: A short circuit provides a very low-resistance path, which can cause a dangerously large current.

topic_questions.text: The resistance of a metallic conductor generally increases when its
topic_questions.explanation: For most metals, resistance increases as temperature increases.

topic_questions.text: A rheostat is used in an electrical circuit to
topic_questions.explanation: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current by changing resistance.

topic_questions.text: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying straight conductor can be determined using the
topic_questions.explanation: The right-hand grip rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.

topic_questions.text: An electric generator converts
topic_questions.explanation: A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction.

topic_questions.text: A transformer is used primarily to
options: change the voltage of alternating current
convert mechanical energy directly into heat
topic_questions.explanation: A transformer changes the voltage of alternating current by electromagnetic induction.

topic_questions.text: A step-up transformer has
options: fewer turns in the secondary coil than in the primary coil
more turns in the secondary coil than in the primary coil
topic_questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more turns on its secondary coil than on its primary coil.

topic_questions.text: The main purpose of earthing an electrical appliance is to
options: provide a safe path for fault current
make it operate without a switch
topic_questions.explanation: Earthing provides a low-resistance path for fault current, helping protect users from electric shock.

topic_questions.text: Which combination correctly represents the relationship between electrical power, current and resistance?
topic_questions.explanation: Electrical power can be expressed as P = I²R.

topic_questions.text: A 4 Ω resistor carries a current of 2 A. The power dissipated in the resistor is
topic_questions.explanation: Using P = I²R, P = 2² × 4 = 16 W.

topic_questions.text: A capacitor is primarily used in a circuit to
topic_questions.explanation: A capacitor stores electrical charge and energy in an electric field.

topic_questions.text: The smallest unit of an element that retains the chemical properties of the element is the
topic_questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains its chemical properties.

topic_questions.text: The negatively charged particle in an atom is the
topic_questions.explanation: An electron carries a negative electric charge.

topic_questions.text: The nucleus of an atom contains
topic_questions.explanation: The atomic nucleus contains positively charged protons and neutral neutrons.

topic_questions.text: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
topic_questions.explanation: The atomic number is defined as the number of protons in the nucleus.

topic_questions.text: The mass number of an atom is the total number of
topic_questions.explanation: Mass number is the sum of the numbers of protons and neutrons.

topic_questions.text: Atoms of the same element having different numbers of neutrons are called
topic_questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different numbers of neutrons.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an isotope of hydrogen?
topic_questions.explanation: Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen containing one proton and one neutron.

topic_questions.text: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when electromagnetic radiation of suitable frequency falls on it is called
topic_questions.explanation: Photoelectric emission is the release of electrons from a material due to incident electromagnetic radiation.

topic_questions.text: The minimum frequency required to eject electrons from a metal surface is called the
topic_questions.explanation: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency needed to cause photoelectric emission from a particular metal.

topic_questions.text: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the frequency of incident light above the threshold frequency increases the
options: maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
topic_questions.explanation: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons increases as the frequency of incident radiation increases above the threshold.

topic_questions.text: Increasing the intensity of light of frequency above the threshold frequency generally increases the
options: number of photoelectrons emitted per second
topic_questions.explanation: At a suitable frequency, greater intensity means more photons strike the surface per second, increasing the number of emitted electrons.

topic_questions.text: The energy of a photon is directly proportional to its
topic_questions.explanation: Photon energy is given by E = hf, so it is directly proportional to frequency.

topic_questions.text: The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to its
topic_questions.explanation: Since E = hc ÷ λ, photon energy is inversely proportional to wavelength.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following has the highest photon energy?
topic_questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the highest frequency and therefore the highest photon energy among these options.

topic_questions.text: The constant represented by h in the equation E = hf is called
topic_questions.explanation: h is Planck's constant, which relates photon energy to frequency.

topic_questions.text: The approximate value of Planck's constant is
topic_questions.explanation: Planck's constant is approximately 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

topic_questions.text: The phenomenon that provides evidence for the particle nature of light is the
topic_questions.explanation: The photoelectric effect demonstrates that light transfers energy in discrete packets called photons.

topic_questions.text: The phenomenon that provides strong evidence for the wave nature of light is
topic_questions.explanation: Interference is a characteristic wave phenomenon and provides evidence for the wave nature of light.

topic_questions.text: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from
topic_questions.explanation: Radioactivity occurs when unstable atomic nuclei spontaneously transform and emit radiation.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is not a common type of nuclear radiation?
topic_questions.explanation: Alpha, beta and gamma are the three principal types of nuclear radiation; ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation but is not a principal nuclear radiation type.

topic_questions.text: An alpha particle is essentially a
topic_questions.explanation: An alpha particle consists of two protons and two neutrons, which is the nucleus of a helium atom.

topic_questions.text: A beta-minus particle is essentially a
topic_questions.explanation: Beta-minus radiation consists of high-speed electrons emitted from unstable nuclei.

topic_questions.text: Gamma radiation consists of
topic_questions.explanation: Gamma radiation consists of high-energy electromagnetic waves.

topic_questions.text: Which nuclear radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
topic_questions.explanation: Gamma radiation has much greater penetrating power than alpha or beta radiation.

topic_questions.text: Which nuclear radiation is most strongly deflected by an electric field?
topic_questions.explanation: Beta particles have a much smaller mass than alpha particles and are therefore deflected more strongly by an electric field.

topic_questions.text: The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time required for
options: half the radioactive nuclei to decay
topic_questions.explanation: Half-life is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

topic_questions.text: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 4 hours. What fraction remains after 8 hours?
topic_questions.explanation: After 4 hours, half remains; after another 4 hours, half of that remains, giving 1/4.

topic_questions.text: A radioactive sample initially contains 800 nuclei. If one half-life has elapsed, the number remaining is
topic_questions.explanation: After one half-life, half the original nuclei remain: 800 ÷ 2 = 400.

topic_questions.text: The activity of a radioactive sample is measured in
topic_questions.explanation: Radioactive activity is measured in becquerels (Bq), where one becquerel represents one decay per second.

topic_questions.text: The process by which a heavy atomic nucleus splits into smaller nuclei is called
topic_questions.explanation: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into smaller nuclei, usually with the release of energy.

topic_questions.text: The process in which light atomic nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus is called
topic_questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion involves the combination of light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus.

topic_questions.text: The energy released in nuclear reactions is mainly associated with a change in
topic_questions.explanation: Nuclear energy is related to changes in mass, according to the mass-energy relationship E = mc².

topic_questions.text: The equation E = mc² expresses the equivalence between
topic_questions.explanation: Einstein's equation shows that mass can be converted into energy and vice versa.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is commonly used as fuel in nuclear fission reactors?
topic_questions.explanation: Uranium-235 is a fissile isotope commonly used as fuel in nuclear reactors.

topic_questions.text: A chain reaction in nuclear fission occurs because the fission of one nucleus can
options: produce neutrons that cause further fission
remove all electrons from the reactor
topic_questions.explanation: Neutrons released during fission can cause other nuclei to undergo fission, producing a chain reaction.

topic_questions.text: A device designed to produce a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction is a
topic_questions.explanation: A nuclear reactor is designed to sustain and control a nuclear fission chain reaction.

topic_questions.text: The main function of control rods in a nuclear reactor is to
options: increase the temperature of the reactor
absorb neutrons and control the chain reaction
topic_questions.explanation: Control rods absorb neutrons and regulate the rate of the fission chain reaction.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a major application of radioisotopes in medicine?
options: Diagnosis and treatment of some diseases
topic_questions.explanation: Radioisotopes are used in medical diagnosis and in certain treatments.

topic_questions.text: Radioactive tracers are useful because their radiation can be
options: seen with the naked eye in every case
stopped by ordinary paper in every case
topic_questions.explanation: Radiation from suitable tracers can be detected externally, allowing their movement or distribution to be monitored.

topic_questions.text: Thermionic emission is the release of
options: electrons from a heated metal surface
topic_questions.explanation: Thermionic emission occurs when electrons gain enough energy to escape from a heated metal surface.

topic_questions.text: A semiconductor has electrical conductivity that is generally
options: between that of a conductor and an insulator
equal to that of a vacuum
topic_questions.explanation: Semiconductors have electrical conductivity intermediate between good conductors and insulators.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a common semiconductor material?
topic_questions.explanation: Silicon is one of the most widely used semiconductor materials.

topic_questions.text: A diode is a semiconductor device that mainly allows current to flow
topic_questions.explanation: A diode conducts readily in its forward direction and strongly restricts current in the reverse direction.

topic_questions.text: A light-emitting diode converts electrical energy mainly into
topic_questions.explanation: An LED converts electrical energy into light energy.

topic_questions.text: A solar cell converts
topic_questions.explanation: A solar cell uses the photovoltaic effect to convert light energy into electrical energy.

topic_questions.text: The atomic model in which electrons occupy specific energy levels around the nucleus was proposed by
topic_questions.explanation: Niels Bohr proposed a model in which electrons occupy specific quantized energy levels.

topic_questions.text: When an electron in an atom moves from a higher energy level to a lower energy level, it
topic_questions.explanation: An electron emits a photon whose energy equals the difference between the two energy levels.

topic_questions.text: When an electron absorbs energy and moves to a higher energy level, the atom is said to be
topic_questions.explanation: An atom is excited when one of its electrons moves to a higher allowed energy level.

topic_questions.text: X-rays are widely used in hospitals mainly for
topic_questions.explanation: X-rays penetrate soft tissue and are useful for imaging bones and certain internal structures.

topic_questions.text: Which radiation is commonly used to sterilize some medical equipment?
topic_questions.explanation: Gamma rays have strong penetrating and ionizing effects and can be used to sterilize medical equipment.

topic_questions.text: The emission of particles or electromagnetic radiation from an unstable nucleus usually results in the formation of
topic_questions.explanation: Radioactive decay transforms an unstable nucleus into a more stable configuration.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following has no electric charge?
topic_questions.explanation: A neutron has zero net electric charge.

topic_questions.text: The charge on a proton is
topic_questions.explanation: A proton carries one positive elementary charge.

topic_questions.text: The charge on an electron is
options: equal to the charge of a neutron
topic_questions.explanation: An electron carries one negative elementary charge.

topic_questions.text: The ability of a material to regain its original shape after removal of an applied force is called
topic_questions.explanation: Elasticity is the property that enables a material to return to its original shape after deformation.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of pressure is
topic_questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa).

topic_questions.text: Pressure is defined as
topic_questions.explanation: Pressure is the normal force acting per unit area.

topic_questions.text: A force of 200 N acts normally on an area of 4 m². The pressure produced is
topic_questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 Pa.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following quantities is a scalar?
topic_questions.explanation: Density has magnitude only and is therefore a scalar quantity.

topic_questions.text: Density is defined as
topic_questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume.

topic_questions.text: A substance has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 200 cm³. Its density is
topic_questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 600 ÷ 200 = 3 g/cm³.

topic_questions.text: The relative density of a substance is the ratio of its density to the density of
topic_questions.explanation: Relative density is the density of a substance divided by the density of water for liquids and solids.

topic_questions.text: An object will float in water if its average density is
options: greater than the density of water
less than the density of water
topic_questions.explanation: An object floats when its average density is less than the density of the fluid.

topic_questions.text: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object is called
topic_questions.explanation: Upthrust is the upward buoyant force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object.

topic_questions.text: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on an immersed body is equal to the
topic_questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced by the immersed body.

topic_questions.text: A body weighs 80 N in air and 50 N when completely immersed in water. Its upthrust is
topic_questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight in air − apparent weight in water = 80 − 50 = 30 N.

topic_questions.text: The instrument commonly used to measure the relative density of liquids is the
topic_questions.explanation: A hydrometer is used to measure the relative density of liquids.

topic_questions.text: The pressure exerted by a liquid at a point depends directly on the
options: surface area of the container only
topic_questions.explanation: Liquid pressure increases with depth.

topic_questions.text: At the same depth in a stationary liquid, the pressure is
options: dependent only on the container shape
topic_questions.explanation: Pressure in a stationary fluid at a given depth acts equally in all directions.

topic_questions.text: The pressure exerted by a liquid at depth h is given by
topic_questions.explanation: Liquid pressure due to depth is given by P = ρgh.

topic_questions.text: A liquid has density 1,000 kg/m³. Taking g as 10 m/s², the pressure due to the liquid at a depth of 2 m is
A barometer is used to measure
topic_questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

topic_questions.text: The standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: Standard atmospheric pressure is approximately 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa.

topic_questions.text: A hydraulic press operates mainly on
topic_questions.explanation: A hydraulic press works by transmitting pressure equally through an enclosed fluid, according to Pascal's principle.

topic_questions.text: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted
topic_questions.explanation: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions.

topic_questions.text: A hydraulic machine has a small piston of area 0.02 m² and a large piston of area 0.2 m². If a force of 100 N is applied to the small piston, the force on the large piston is
topic_questions.explanation: Using F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, F₂ = 100 × 0.2 ÷ 0.02 = 1,000 N.

topic_questions.text: The resistance of a fluid to the relative motion of its layers is called
topic_questions.explanation: Viscosity is the internal resistance of a fluid to flow.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of dynamic viscosity is
topic_questions.explanation: The SI unit of dynamic viscosity is pascal-second (Pa s).

topic_questions.text: Which of the following liquids has the greatest viscosity under ordinary conditions?
topic_questions.explanation: Honey has a much higher resistance to flow than the other listed liquids.

topic_questions.text: Surface tension causes a liquid surface to behave approximately like
topic_questions.explanation: Surface tension makes a liquid surface behave somewhat like a stretched elastic membrane.

topic_questions.text: Small insects can walk on the surface of water mainly because of
topic_questions.explanation: Surface tension provides support that can allow small insects to remain on the water surface.

topic_questions.text: Capillary action is the rise or fall of a liquid in a narrow tube mainly due to
topic_questions.explanation: Capillary action results from the combined effects of adhesive and cohesive forces.

topic_questions.text: Water rises in a clean glass capillary tube because
options: adhesion between water and glass is strong
topic_questions.explanation: Water rises because the adhesive force between water and glass is stronger than the cohesive force within the water.

topic_questions.text: Hooke's law states that, within the elastic limit, extension is proportional to
topic_questions.explanation: Hooke's law states that extension is directly proportional to applied force within the elastic limit.

topic_questions.text: A spring extends by 4 cm when a force of 8 N is applied. Its spring constant is
topic_questions.explanation: Using F = ke, k = 8 ÷ 0.04 = 200 N/m.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of the spring constant is
topic_questions.explanation: From F = ke, the unit of spring constant is newton per metre (N/m).

topic_questions.text: The point beyond which a material no longer returns completely to its original shape is associated with the
topic_questions.explanation: The elastic limit is the maximum deformation up to which a material can return to its original shape.

topic_questions.text: The ability of a material to be drawn into wires is called
topic_questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability of a material to be drawn into wires.

topic_questions.text: The ability of a material to be hammered into thin sheets is called
topic_questions.explanation: Malleability is the ability of a material to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets.

topic_questions.text: A material that breaks easily without significant deformation is described as
topic_questions.explanation: A brittle material fractures with little or no permanent deformation.

topic_questions.text: The gravitational force acting on an object is called its
topic_questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object.

topic_questions.text: An object has a mass of 5 kg. Taking g as 10 m/s², its weight is
topic_questions.explanation: Weight = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N.

topic_questions.text: The mass of an object remains constant when it is taken from Earth to the Moon, but its
topic_questions.explanation: Mass is constant, while weight changes because gravitational acceleration differs on the Moon.

topic_questions.text: The principle of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be
options: created nor destroyed in an ordinary physical process
topic_questions.explanation: In ordinary physical processes, mass is conserved and cannot simply be created or destroyed.

topic_questions.text: The pressure exerted by a solid is greatest when the same force acts on the
topic_questions.explanation: Since pressure = force ÷ area, the pressure is greatest when the area is smallest.

topic_questions.text: A sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt knife because the sharp edge
options: has a smaller contact area and produces greater pressure
reduces the applied force to zero
topic_questions.explanation: A sharp edge has a smaller contact area, producing greater pressure for the same applied force.

topic_questions.text: The buoyant force acting on an object immersed in a fluid acts
options: towards the centre of the Earth
topic_questions.explanation: The pressure difference in a fluid produces an upward buoyant force called upthrust.

topic_questions.text: A body sinks in a liquid when its average density is
options: less than that of the liquid
greater than that of the liquid
topic_questions.explanation: An object sinks when its average density is greater than the density of the liquid.

topic_questions.text: When a body is completely submerged in a liquid, the upthrust is equal to the weight of the
topic_questions.explanation: According to Archimedes' principle, upthrust equals the weight of the liquid displaced.

topic_questions.text: The flow of a fluid in which adjacent layers move smoothly without significant mixing is called
topic_questions.explanation: Laminar flow occurs when fluid moves in smooth, orderly layers.

topic_questions.text: For an incompressible fluid flowing steadily through a pipe, if the cross-sectional area decreases, the fluid speed generally
topic_questions.explanation: By the continuity principle, fluid speed increases when the cross-sectional area decreases.

topic_questions.text: The continuity equation for an incompressible fluid flowing through a pipe is
topic_questions.explanation: For steady incompressible flow, the product of cross-sectional area and speed remains constant.

topic_questions.text: A liquid flows through a pipe of area 4 cm² at 2 m/s. If the pipe narrows to an area of 2 cm², the new speed is
topic_questions.explanation: Using A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, v₂ = 4 × 2 ÷ 2 = 4 m/s.

topic_questions.text: According to Bernoulli's principle, where the speed of a flowing fluid increases, its pressure generally
topic_questions.explanation: For steady flow under suitable conditions, an increase in fluid speed is associated with a decrease in pressure.

topic_questions.text: The upward lift of an aircraft wing is partly explained by
topic_questions.explanation: The pressure difference associated with airflow around the wing contributes to aerodynamic lift and is explained partly using Bernoulli's principle.

topic_questions.text: A fluid with a high viscosity generally flows
topic_questions.explanation: High viscosity means greater resistance to flow, so the fluid generally flows more slowly.

topic_questions.text: The density of a substance is 2,500 kg/m³. Its relative density is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: Relative density = 2,500 ÷ 1,000 = 2.5, taking water density as 1,000 kg/m³.

topic_questions.text: An object displaces 0.003 m³ of water. Taking the density of water as 1,000 kg/m³ and g as 10 m/s², the upthrust is
Work is said to be done when a force acting on a body causes
options: a displacement in the direction of the force
topic_questions.explanation: Work is done when a force causes displacement in the direction of the force.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of work is the
topic_questions.explanation: The SI unit of work and energy is the joule (J).

topic_questions.text: A force of 20 N moves an object through 5 m in the direction of the force. The work done is
topic_questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance = 20 × 5 = 100 J.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a form of kinetic energy?
options: Energy stored in a stretched spring
Energy possessed by a moving car
Energy stored in a raised object
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.

topic_questions.text: The energy possessed by a body because of its position above the ground is called
topic_questions.explanation: A body raised above the ground possesses gravitational potential energy.

topic_questions.text: A body of mass 4 kg moves with a velocity of 5 m/s. Its kinetic energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 mv² = 1/2 × 4 × 5² = 50 J.

topic_questions.text: A 2 kg object is raised through a vertical height of 10 m. If g = 10 m/s², the gain in gravitational potential energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J.

topic_questions.text: Power is defined as the rate of doing
topic_questions.explanation: Power is the rate at which work is done.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of power is the
topic_questions.explanation: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).

topic_questions.text: A machine does 600 J of work in 20 s. Its power output is
topic_questions.explanation: Power = work ÷ time = 600 ÷ 20 = 30 W.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a unit of energy?
topic_questions.explanation: The joule is the SI unit of energy.

topic_questions.text: A force of 50 N acts on an object through a distance of 2 m at an angle of 60° to the direction of motion. The work done is
Which quantity is conserved in an isolated system when no energy is transferred to the surroundings?
topic_questions.explanation: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.

topic_questions.text: A stone falls from a height. As it falls, its gravitational potential energy is mainly converted into
topic_questions.explanation: As the stone falls, gravitational potential energy is converted mainly into kinetic energy.

topic_questions.text: A 10 kg object is lifted vertically through 5 m. If g = 10 m/s², the work done against gravity is
topic_questions.explanation: Work done = mgh = 10 × 10 × 5 = 500 J.

topic_questions.text: The kinetic energy of a body depends on its
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is given by 1/2 mv², so it depends on mass and velocity.

topic_questions.text: If the speed of a body is doubled while its mass remains constant, its kinetic energy becomes
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to v². Doubling velocity makes the kinetic energy four times larger.

topic_questions.text: If the mass of a moving body is doubled while its velocity remains constant, its kinetic energy becomes
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is directly proportional to mass when velocity is constant.

topic_questions.text: A 5 kg body moves at 4 m/s. Its kinetic energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 × 5 × 4² = 40 J.

topic_questions.text: A 3 kg object is raised through 4 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², its gain in potential energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh = 3 × 10 × 4 = 120 J.

topic_questions.text: A machine has an input energy of 500 J and an output energy of 400 J. Its efficiency is
topic_questions.explanation: Efficiency = output ÷ input × 100 = 400 ÷ 500 × 100 = 80%.

topic_questions.text: A machine uses 2,000 J of energy and produces 1,500 J of useful output energy. The energy wasted is
topic_questions.explanation: Wasted energy = input energy - useful output = 2,000 - 1,500 = 500 J.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is an example of chemical potential energy?
topic_questions.explanation: Fuel stores energy chemically, which can be released during combustion.

topic_questions.text: A person carries a load horizontally at constant height and constant speed. Ignoring air resistance, the work done by gravity on the load is
topic_questions.explanation: Gravity acts vertically while the displacement is horizontal, so the angle is 90° and the work done by gravity is zero.

topic_questions.text: A force acts on a body but produces no displacement. The work done by the force is
topic_questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force. With zero displacement, work done is zero.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following has the greatest effect on the kinetic energy of a body?
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy depends strongly on velocity because it is proportional to the square of velocity.

topic_questions.text: A machine lifts a 200 N load through 5 m in 10 s. The useful power developed is
