topic_questions.text: Which of the following statements about power is correct?
options: Power is the rate of doing work
Power is the total distance travelled
Power is the force divided by mass
Power is the mass multiplied by velocity
topic_questions.explanation: Power measures how quickly work is done.

topic_questions.text: Two machines do the same amount of work. Machine A takes 5 s while machine B takes 10 s. Which machine has greater power?
topic_questions.explanation: For the same work, the machine that takes less time has greater power.

topic_questions.text: A 1 kg object moves with a speed of 10 m/s. Its kinetic energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 × 1 × 10² = 50 J.

topic_questions.text: A 20 kg object is raised through 2 m. If g = 10 m/s², the work done against gravity is
topic_questions.explanation: Work done = mgh = 20 × 10 × 2 = 400 J.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following energy conversions occurs in a hydroelectric power station?
options: Gravitational potential energy to electrical energy
topic_questions.explanation: Water stored at height has gravitational potential energy, which is converted into electrical energy.

topic_questions.text: The efficiency of a machine is 75%. If its input energy is 800 J, the useful output energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Useful output = 75/100 × 800 = 600 J.

topic_questions.text: A machine has an output power of 600 W and an input power of 750 W. Its efficiency is
topic_questions.explanation: Efficiency = output power ÷ input power × 100 = 600 ÷ 750 × 100 = 80%.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is not a mechanical form of energy?
topic_questions.explanation: Chemical energy is stored in chemical substances and is not a mechanical form of energy.

topic_questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward. At its highest point, its kinetic energy is
topic_questions.explanation: At the highest point, the instantaneous velocity is zero, so its kinetic energy is zero.

topic_questions.text: As a ball falls freely from a height, its gravitational potential energy
options: remains the only form of energy
topic_questions.explanation: During free fall, gravitational potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases.

topic_questions.text: A force of 40 N acts on a body through 3 m at an angle of 90° to the displacement. The work done is
topic_questions.explanation: Work = Fd cos 90° = 0 J.

topic_questions.text: A force of 30 N acts at an angle of 0° to the displacement of 4 m. The work done is
topic_questions.explanation: Work = Fd cos 0° = 30 × 4 × 1 = 120 J.

topic_questions.text: The work done in lifting a 50 N object through a vertical height of 6 m is
topic_questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance = 50 × 6 = 300 J.

topic_questions.text: A 2 kg object moves with a speed of 6 m/s. Its kinetic energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = 1/2 × 2 × 6² = 36 J.

topic_questions.text: If no energy is lost, the total mechanical energy of a freely falling object
topic_questions.explanation: When there is no energy loss, the sum of kinetic and potential energies remains constant.

topic_questions.text: An electric motor has a power rating of 1,000 W. This means it can
options: do 1,000 J of work every second
exert a force of 1,000 N only
use 1,000 kg of mass every second
topic_questions.explanation: A power of 1,000 W means the motor can transfer or do 1,000 J of energy per second.

topic_questions.text: A 500 W machine operates for 20 s. The work done by the machine is
topic_questions.explanation: Work = power × time = 500 × 20 = 10,000 J.

topic_questions.text: A body has 200 J of kinetic energy and 300 J of gravitational potential energy. Its total mechanical energy is
topic_questions.explanation: Total mechanical energy = kinetic energy + potential energy = 200 + 300 = 500 J.

topic_questions.text: A machine receives 2,500 J of energy and wastes 500 J. Its efficiency is
Which of the following would increase the gravitational potential energy of an object?
topic_questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy is mgh, so increasing height increases the potential energy.

topic_questions.text: A force of 80 N moves an object through 5 m in the direction of the force. What is the work done?
topic_questions.explanation: Work done = force × distance = 80 × 5 = 400 J.

topic_questions.text: A force is best defined as a
topic_questions.explanation: A force is a push or pull that can change the state of motion or shape of an object.

topic_questions.text: The SI unit of force is the
topic_questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

topic_questions.text: A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg. What is the acceleration produced?
topic_questions.explanation: Using F = ma, acceleration = F ÷ m = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 m/s².

topic_questions.text: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act at right angles to each other. What is their resultant force?
topic_questions.explanation: Resultant force = square root of (6² + 8²) = square root of 100 = 10 N.

topic_questions.text: A body is said to be in equilibrium when the
options: resultant force acting on it is zero
body has no acceleration due to gravity
topic_questions.explanation: A body is in translational equilibrium when the resultant force acting on it is zero.

topic_questions.text: Which of the following is a contact force?
topic_questions.explanation: Friction acts between surfaces in contact and is therefore a contact force.

topic_questions.text: The weight of a body is the
options: force with which the Earth attracts the body
topic_questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force acting on a body and is given by W = mg.

topic_questions.text: A body of mass 5 kg is acted upon by a gravitational acceleration of 10 m/s². Its weight is
topic_questions.explanation: Weight = mg = 5 × 10 = 50 N.

topic_questions.text: The tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of motion is called
topic_questions.explanation: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist changes in its state of rest or motion.

topic_questions.text: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of
topic_questions.explanation: Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a resultant external force, so it is called the law of inertia.

topic_questions.text: A force of 20 N acts on a mass of 4 kg. The acceleration is
topic_questions.explanation: Using F = ma, a = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

topic_questions.text: Which of the following forces always acts towards the centre of the Earth?
topic_questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force on a body and acts vertically towards the centre of the Earth.

topic_questions.text: The force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact is
topic_questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion or the tendency of relative motion between contacting surfaces.

topic_questions.text: A force of 15 N acts east while another force of 15 N acts west on the same body. The resultant force is
topic_questions.explanation: The forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so they cancel and the resultant is zero.

topic_questions.text: The turning effect of a force about a point is called
topic_questions.explanation: The turning effect of a force about a point is called its moment.

topic_questions.text: The moment of a force about a point is calculated as
topic_questions.explanation: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
